meta.what: Round 39 research input. (1) Profits of companies from each home country operating in Russia (while still foreign-owned), the share that reached the home country as dividends, the share trapped in Russia, the no-war level and the change; (2) income of foreign partners in Russian LNG and upstream projects (TotalEnergies, CNPC, Silk Road Fund, Mitsui, Mitsubishi, SODECO, Indian state firms, BP, Shell, ExxonMobil, Wintershall Dea, OMV).
meta.units: EUR bn, nominal. USD at ECB annual averages; RUB per EUR 87.2 (2021), 72.5, 92.2, 100.3, 94, 93 (2026), as company_flows.json and company_taxes_r6.json.
meta.years: 2021-2025 calendar years; 2026 = January-August, NOT annualised (the builder must not apply FRAC again).
meta.sign: change > 0 = the home country's owners earned MORE from Russia than without the war = toward Russia (same sign as company taxes paid in Russia). change < 0 = earned less = toward Ukraine. The builder stores it like add_extra(): money toward Russia, sign flipped.

series.actual_profit: net profit after Russian tax attributable to owners from the country, firms still foreign-owned that year (KSE in-scope definition: non-exited plus f x exited cohort)
series.dividends_reached_home: actual_profit x the country's payout ratio that year (OECD FDI income: dividends / (dividends + reinvested earnings))
series.trapped: actual_profit x (pre-war payout - actual payout): profit that would have been paid out but stayed in Russia (type-C accounts, dividend bans for 'unfriendly' owners). 0 for other owners
series.counted_actual: dividends + normal retention + trapped x value weight p (low 0.10 / central 0.35 / high 1.0): the owners' gain
series.nowar_profit: base_2018_2021 x company trend multiplier (trend2.json global; the builder should use the country multiplier where reliable, as for company taxes)
series.nowar_counted: nowar_profit with the profit lost by exiters counted only above the normal return on their sale proceeds (share s_exit 0.6, 0.4-0.85)

meta.method: Profit = in-scope profit tax (company_taxes_r6.json) x KSE's ratio of net income to profit tax for in-scope firms that year (KSE80 by status) x a country factor from KSE's Figure 4 profits by HQ country 2021-2023 (square root of the raw ratio, 0.5-2.0). Company reports replace the model where they exist: Raiffeisen's Russia profit after tax (country-by-country tables 2021-2024; 2024 and 2025 before the Rasperia court charges, which are in the seizure marker), OTP Russia 2024-2025. For 12 OECD countries with an official split (DEU, ITA, AUT, FIN, SWE, DNK, KOR, CZE, POL, ESP, BEL, NOR) the central is the mean of the model and OECD direct-investment equity income from Russia (2018-2024; DEU and AUT net of the upstream JVs in item 4).
meta.trapped_profits_rule: Recommended: count dividends that reached the home country in full, normal retention in full, and profit trapped in Russia at a value weight p = 0.35 (0.10-1.0): what an 'unfriendly' owner can actually get for a rouble kept in Russia (sale at >= 50-60% discount and a 15-35% exit fee gives 0.26-0.43, plus a small option on normalisation). The rest (0.65 of trapped profit, EUR 11bn of 17.3bn trapped 2022-Aug 2026) is a gain Russia keeps: a marker beside 'seized' and 'exits' in c['taken'], not in the totals. Owners of non-'unfriendly' countries (China, Turkiye, India for its own firms, UAE ...) face no type-C restriction: p = 1. Accrual in full (p = 1) would be the textbook 'seller's gain' but credits owners with money Russia can and does take; cash only (p = 0) ignores that the claim keeps some value.

overlaps.company_taxes_r6: No overlap: profits here are after Russian tax; taxes stay where they are. Same scope (foreign-owned while not exited; Unipro and Fortum out from May 2023 through the in-scope profit tax).
overlaps.exits_and_seized_markers: Not in the totals, so counting lost profits of exiters is not counted twice; to be consistent, an exiter's lost profit counts only above the normal return on its sale proceeds (s_exit 0.6). Seized companies' lost profit counts like their lost taxes. RBI's Rasperia charges (2024 provision 840m, 2025 debit) are left out of RBI profit because the 1.87bn is in the seizure marker.
overlaps.net_gain_on_goods_sold: Exports by a parent to its Russian subsidiary count in trade at the seller's net gain; the subsidiary's own profit in Russia is separate value added. Transfer pricing can move profit between them; not corrected (small against the totals).
overlaps.lng_foreign_share: The pipeline keeps only 60% of LNG profit after tax as Russia's (net_gain_russia-notes.md). Item 4 credits the foreign partners' own change; it adds nothing to Russia's side and does not need a correction there.
overlaps.crude_stakes: Russia's crude net gain ignores foreign stakes (BP-Rosneft, Indian Vankor/Taas-Yuryakh). Trapped amounts therefore get weight 0 for BP and 0.5 for India; the paid Indian dividends of 2021-2022 are tiny against Russia's crude gain.
overlaps.upstream_in_oecd: OECD FDI income of Germany, Austria, France and Japan contains the upstream stakes of item 4; Germany's and Austria's OECD figures are used net of them, France and Japan are not blended.

meta.builder_hint: Store item 1 per country as c['company']['profits'] (same base/bmul machinery as company taxes, base_2018_2021 = true) or as add_extra('coprofits', ...); item 4 per home country as add_extra('lngpartners', ...). Use 'change' (already against the no-war level, 2026 Jan-Aug) or rebuild from counted_actual and nowar_profit with the country's trend2 multiplier. Positive change = toward Russia. Put 0.65 x trapped (central) into c['taken'] as 'trapped profits'.

Value weight 0 (0-0.2): BP wrote the stake off and the pipeline already counts all Rosneft profit as Russia's (crude net gain ignores foreign stakes), so counting any of it for the UK would count it twice.
